title: Tenant handoff ephemeral arena leak and graceful evict rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers (hosted burst workloads and one Dedicated tenant) reported recurrent GPU OOMs over multi-hour sessions. Root cause analysis points to an intermittent race during tenant handoff + async snapshot commit that leaves ephemeral tensor arenas and KV-cache fence objects un-freed. Over time these orphaned arenas accumulate, producing severe GPU memory fragmentation and eventual OOM on nodes serving long-lived sessions. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigations, and rollout of a runtime patch that adds explicit fence reconciliation and a graceful-evict canary rollout.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a hosted node configured for burst tenancy with prefetch watermark enabled
2) Start 30 concurrent long-running chat sessions that perform repeated prefix appends and attention cache growth (avg seq_len 2048 per session)
3) Trigger tenant handoff by simulating tenant shutdown/reconnect loops (kill-restart client + force session transfer)
4) Observe GPU resident set growth (nvidia-smi) and increasing count of 'arena' allocations in runtime gc logs
5) After ~2-5 hours, node reports OOM and sessions fail with allocation error E_GPU_OOM
investigation_notes: Initial alert: hosted customer A reported spike in 503s and OOMs at 2025-03-08 04:12 UTC; Dedicated customer B later reproduced on a reserved pool node
Heap snapshot (lldb/nvprof) showed multiple 'TensorArena' allocations with identical base IDs but no corresponding free calls after snapshot commit
Trace logs show async snapshot commit path takes a fast-path that skips 'fence-resolve' when retry_count > 0; cadence of tenant handoffs correlates with leak windows
KV-cache's fence objects are reference-counted; we found a code path where fence moved between threads without incrementing refcount leading to a lost finalizer
Fragmentation: small unreachable holes between large allocated arenas -> allocator can't coalesce because fence metadata pinned adjacent slabs
Metric anomalies: persistent rise in runtime.memory.arena_count and host.gpu.fragmentation_ratio preceding OOM by 30-90 minutes
Reproducible locally with a stress harness (runtime/tools/tenancy_replay) when latency injection added to snapshot commit
Crashdumps: one crashdump showed device-side allocation failure but host process still had ~6GB of non-accounted device memory in tracked arenas
decision_and_plan: Short-term mitigation (hotfix): Add explicit periodic fence reconciliation job that runs on node leader every 5 minutes to detect and free orphaned arenas. Backported to 1.20-hotfix branch.
Root fix (runtime-1.21): Ensure atomic refcount increment on fence handoff code path and make async snapshot commit await fence reconciliation on teardown path when handoff_count > 0
Canary rollout: staged canary across 3 host pools: small internal pool -> hosted non-production -> hosted prod with rate limit 1% -> Dedicated reserved nodes (smoke first)
Feature flag: runtime.enable_fence_reconcile (default true on canary) and runtime.strict_refcount (default false, enabled in next step after monitoring)
Customer remediation: advise customers to perform rolling session restarts if they see fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 while we push hotfix
Post-release: add an automated regression test to the nightly harness that exercises rapid tenant handoffs under latency injection
rollback_and_mitigation_steps: If canary shows regression in latency or increased transient errors, flip runtime.enable_fence_reconcile=false and roll back runtime image to runtime-1.20.9-hotfix
Emergency kill: drain affected nodes (nodectl cordon && nodectl drain) to prevent further OOMs and shift traffic to backup pools
Manual memory reclaim: restart serving runtime on affected nodes (low-impact window) to reclaim orphaned device memory
Notify customers via status page: post incident update with steps taken and expected ETA for full patch
deploy_plan: 1) Merge PR#4321 to runtime/main with feature flags and unit tests (done)
2) Build runtime-1.21-canary image and deploy to internal canary pool (2025-03-17)
3) Monitor canary metrics (memory.arena_count, gpu.fragmentation_ratio, tail-latency) for 48h
4) If stable, promote to hosted non-prod for 24h, then to 1% prod traffic and Dedicated smoke nodes
5) After 72h of stable signals, enable strict_refcount and roll to 100%
6) Postmortem and follow-up tasks scheduled in next cycle

Add regression harness test and incorporate into PR gating (owner: Marco Alvarez)
Create alert runbook entry for rapid tenant-handoff leaks (oncall playbook)
Audit other async-commit paths for similar refcount assumptions (owner: runtime-dev lead)

Follow-up: evaluate allocator changes to reduce fragmentation susceptibility (research spike)
